parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by contrast in an X-ray image.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
X-rays of intensity *I*₀ are incident normally on a structure, as shown in Fig. 10.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Material P has a linear attenuation coefficient of 0.35 cm⁻¹.
The X-rays emerging from the structure in region A have an intensity of 0.05*I*₀.
parts.text: Show that the intensity of the X-rays emerging in region B is 0.13*I*₀.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the linear attenuation coefficient *μ* of material Q.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use the information in (b)(i) to suggest why the X-rays emerging from the structure form an image that has poor contrast.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain how X-rays are used in computed tomography (CT) scanning to produce a three-dimensional image of an internal structure.

figures.caption: Fig. 10.1
figures.alt: A diagram shows horizontal incident and detected X-rays passing through a structure made of material P with a narrow central section of material Q, with regions A and B marked.
